one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience bank's gain is absorbed by an instruction optimized on the same training episodes, separated from the ceiling effect that any accuracy-matched but episode-content-free instruction would also produce, using a 'headroom curve' of information-free instructions, a train-half provenance crossover with a planted half-specific positive control, and a token-matched compiled-bank arm.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) is the live threat: it already runs ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on the same 528/267 training trajectories across three backbones including Qwen3.5-27B, and reports GEPA within a couple of points of ReasoningBank (+1.2 vs +3.6) with no automatic method positive in every cell. That table already licenses this paper's practical takeaway ('the optimizer is a comparable container, and neither is reliable'), so the marginal contribution is the decomposition, not the finding. The proposal correctly identifies what EvoAgentBench lacks - combined I1xM cells, token matching, paired statistics, a compiled arm, provenance - and those absences are real. MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the second threat and is the name a reviewer will say first: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint on one training set is exactly the two-container ablation, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent pre-empts the qualitative answer here. A compounding weakness: Risk 14 refuses to re-measure any published number, so the study audits an evaluation template using its own re-implemented ExpeL/ReasoningBank banks. The track brief says a measurement contribution 'needs to overturn or qualify specific existing results to be interesting'; as written this paper qualifies no published result, only its own bank.
strongest_objection: The primary endpoint's identification assumption is false as stated and untested. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) treats memory's marginal gain as a function of no-memory accuracy alone, estimated from only three non-baseline points that are not even the same kind of intervention: H1 (an evidence-citation line), H2 ('decompose, search each, verify'), and I0+3, which is not an instruction at all but a search-budget increase that plausibly substitutes for memory through an entirely different channel (fewer wasted calls rather than better priors). Two prompts at equal aggregate accuracy leave different residual unsolved sets, and memory's marginal gain depends on the composition of that residual, not its size - so g_H(l1) is not the counterfactual gain of a non-absorbing instruction at level l1, and a positive Delta_abs is equally consistent with GEPA's prompt merely shifting which instances remain unsolved, with no episode content absorbed. Worse, the between-instruction scatter of g at matched level is exactly the null distribution Delta_abs must beat, and with three points at SE ~0.8-1.15pt each it cannot be estimated. The pre-registered primary comparator is anyway the single nearest member I_H*, so the 'curve' is decoration and the confirmatory test is a two-point contrast between one hand-picked generic instruction and one optimized instruction. The arithmetic then makes it worse: the 2pt claim threshold sits below the proposal's own stated MDE of 2.9pt and at the ~2pt treatment-free floor it computes in Measurement (c), and no null replicate of Delta_abs itself exists (cell 10 replicates only g at I0). A 2pt Delta_abs therefore cannot clear the rule 'no effect is claimed unless it exceeds both its test threshold and the 95th percentile of the relevant floor' - the confirmatory result is designed to be inconclusive at its own threshold.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Expand the information-free family to at least six members spanning the accuracy range, and either drop I0+3 from the curve or model it separately, since a budget change is not an instruction and its interaction with memory is mechanistically different; then report the residual scatter of g around the fitted curve and use that scatter - not sampling SE alone - as the null distribution for Delta_abs. (2) Add a genuine null replicate of the primary endpoint: compute Delta_abs between two information-free instructions that land at matched levels, where the true value is zero, at n=1,500; without this the 2pt threshold is uncalibrated. (3) Add an instance-composition diagnostic to the paired analysis - report the Jaccard overlap of the solved sets of I_H* and I1_ab and re-express Delta_abs conditional on the shared residual set - so the reader can see whether level-matching also matched what was left to fix. (4) Promote cell 18 (D_opt and the MIPROv2-style joint J) from Tier 1 to Tier 0 and raise the claim threshold above the achieved MDE, or buy power with more optimizer seeds rather than more Tier-1 cells. (5) Recover at least one published number: run the screened bank under one target paper's own reported setting, even at reduced n, so the audit attaches to a real claim rather than only to a self-built bank.
missing_baseline: The optimized static-demonstration container as a must-ship arm. D_opt and the MIPROv2-style joint instruction+demonstration prompt J are cell 18, sit at Tier 1, and are third in the Tier-1 cut order - so the most likely published outcome has them absent. The title asserts memory is 'just an un-optimized prompt', but a retrieved-experience bank is shaped like the demonstration slot, and instruction-only GEPA is not that slot's representative; MIPROv2 already reports that the instruction/demonstration split is task-dependent, which is precisely the alternative explanation this design leaves open. If J x M0 matches or beats I1_ab x M_ab, the paper's finding is about the demonstration container, not about memory being redundant with instructions, and the headline has to change. A second, cheaper omission: no compute-matched sampling baseline (self-consistency / best-of-n at memory's token budget) - I0+3 raises search calls only, so 'spend memory's budget elsewhere' is tested through one channel out of two.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually strong for a proposal and should be credited: dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), stated query counts and channels, by-id verification for 54 IDs, a committed scan record with a SHA256 for the closest work's extracted text, an explicit retraction of v2's overclaim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other', and a correction of a web snippet that had misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6. I know of no preprint that already makes the specific Delta_abs claim - absorption measured against a level-matched information-free control - and EvoAgentBench, the nearest, is handled honestly rather than hidden. Three real weaknesses. First, arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every citation rests on web-search snippets plus one PI-supplied PDF; the entire novelty argument against the closest work is a single-source chain with no independent channel, which is the same failure mode that produced v2's false retractions. Second, arXiv 2608.14036 - the skills-vs-Workflow-Memory paper, i.e. the single most likely place a compiled-block-vs-live-retrieval comparison already exists - has an unopened appendix that is merely 'flagged'; that is the collision that would gut prediction 4 and cell 9, and it is unchecked. Third, and most damaging, the proposal admits that the design primitive it is most proud of - a held-out-episode provenance crossover asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw - was never searched for and is only on the pre-freeze list. Novelty for the crossover instrument is therefore currently unestablished by the proposal's own account, and the contamination / data-attribution literature is a plausible place for it to already live.
